response.message: We're building an authenticated AWS chat assistant for synthetic users. I've drawn the full flow: sign-in, API, a chat Lambda, per-user conversation storage, a Bedrock model with size limits, and a human escalation queue. Our first local test can use a scripted fake model to check user isolation, size limits, delete behaviour, escalation and recovery when the model fails, but it says nothing about real answer quality, model access or IAM, which need a later test in a real account. Which country should the conversation data stay in, so we can pick an AWS region?

proposal.title: First end-to-end AWS conversational assistant sketch
proposal.body: Scope: an authenticated chat assistant for synthetic users with per-user conversation state, bounded context, a Bedrock model, recovery when the model fails and a human escalation path. External actions are out of scope. Assumptions: the region and country are not yet chosen. The Bedrock model ID, model access and quotas have not been verified. Native generators do not yet cover this chat Lambda, the conversation table or the escalation queue, so those parts still need engineering work. This is a design intent only. Nothing has been deployed or validated.

data.label: Synthetic user (browser)
data.description: A synthetic test user in a browser. This is a client reference and is not provisioned.

data.label: Chat web app
data.description: Hosts the chat UI from private S3 assets. Signs in with authorization code plus PKCE and calls the chat API with an access token.

data.label: User sign-in
data.description: A user pool with admin-created synthetic users and MFA. Issues JWTs whose subject defines who owns each conversation.

data.label: Chat API
data.description: An HTTP API with a JWT authorizer, request size limits and throttling. It rejects anonymous calls.

data.label: Chat orchestrator
data.description: Uses the JWT subject as the owner key and never trusts a user ID sent in the request. Builds a bounded context window from recent turns, enforces input and output limits, and calls the model with retries and timeouts. If the model fails, it returns a recoverable 'try again' response without losing the stored turn. It also handles conversation delete and escalation, and owns its execution role and logs.

data.label: Conversation store
data.description: Partition key: owner subject. Sort key: conversation and turn. Encrypted at rest. Delete removes every turn in the conversation. Optional TTL is still to be decided.

data.label: Foundation model
data.description: A direct foundation model through Converse. The model ID, access, region support and quotas are not yet verified. Local tests replace it with scripted responses.

data.label: Escalation queue
data.description: Receives an escalation record holding a snapshot of the user-approved conversation context. Encrypted, with a dead-letter queue for failed handling.

data.label: Human support reviewer
data.description: A person who picks up escalations. The tooling and access model are still to be decided.

data.label: Logs and alarms
data.description: Lambda and API metrics, a model-error alarm and an escalation DLQ alarm. Logs exclude message content.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Without this, one user could read another user's chats.
requirementDrafts.basis: User acceptance criterion: "One user cannot read another conversation".
requirementDrafts.statement: A user can only read, continue or delete conversations owned by their authenticated subject. Requests for another user's conversation are denied.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Size limits control cost and latency, and stop unbounded prompts. The exact limits shown are proposed defaults, not confirmed values.
requirementDrafts.basis: User acceptance criterion: "Context and response sizes are bounded".
requirementDrafts.statement: Input, context window and model output have enforced maximum sizes. Oversized requests are rejected with a clear error.

requirementDrafts.rationale: A model outage must not lose or corrupt conversation state.
requirementDrafts.basis: User acceptance criterion: "Model outage produces a recoverable response".
requirementDrafts.statement: When the model fails or times out, the user gets a recoverable response and the stored conversation stays intact for a retry.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Users need real deletion, not just hiding. How escalation copies are retained is still an open question.
requirementDrafts.basis: User acceptance criterion: "Deleting a conversation removes its stored context".
requirementDrafts.statement: Deleting a conversation removes all of its stored turns and context from the conversation store.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Reviewers need the context the user approved, and only that context.
requirementDrafts.basis: User acceptance criterion: "Escalation retains the approved conversation context".
requirementDrafts.statement: Escalation sends a snapshot of the user-approved conversation context to the human review queue, and that snapshot is retained there.

request.message:
Act as a patient architecture consultant and teacher. Start with the exact evidence state. If blocked before checks, explicitly say runtime tests have not run and the design is not yet validated. An empty failures list NEVER means a sound, complete or correct design. Celebrate only named checks that actually passed. Explain the most important remaining issue in plain language and help the user make progress. Do not just recite a checklist or demand that a junior developer repair product internals. Offer a concrete supported correction when possible; otherwise ask one focused question and explain why its answer matters. Help improve this architecture from its current emulation results. Diagnose the first actionable finding. Propose a minimal supported architecture correction only when requirements already justify it; otherwise ask one precise question.
Preserve all required components, existing systems, IDs, established service choices, access boundaries and requirements. Never clear unfinished-work gates, remove workload scope, weaken tests or invent successful validation. A graph proposal cannot repair generator/runtime source or an emulator defect: identify that as product engineering work with a reproducer. Model output is not test evidence. A local emulation pass is not a cloud plan or deployment. After an applied correction, rerun emulation on the new artifact; do not reuse this result.
